title: How to effectively communicate your code of ethics: An empirical study using a cluster randomized control trial experiment
abstract: Organizations often communicate codes of ethics without knowing whether those communications improve employees’ understanding. This study uses a cluster-randomized field experiment at a Mexican pawnshop chain, involving 519 workers, to evaluate communication about an existing code. The tested communication did not produce a statistically significant improvement in workers’ understanding of the code. The results highlight the difference between distributing an ethics policy and ensuring that employees comprehend it.
